page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance divergence between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show poor performance. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests, consistently rank in the average tier. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks, along with PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations, also falls within the average range.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is defined by its dedicated physical core allocation and balanced resource density, though it utilizes an older generation Intel Xeon processor. The primary tradeoff is the low single-threaded execution speed compared to modern architectures, which is offset by reliable multi-threaded scaling. This profile makes the instance suitable for multi-threaded workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations, while it is less suited for single-threaded processing or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance utilizing a KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor offering 16 dedicated physical cores at 2.5 GHz and 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast: single-core metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression, rank in the lower percentiles, whereas multi-core benchmarks, including multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and Redis SET operations, consistently achieve average tier results. This hardware profile provides a stable multi-threaded environment, making it suitable for workloads like static web serving, software compilation, and database operations, though it presents a clear tradeoff in single-threaded execution speed.
